action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and show where the polyradiculoneuropathy lies; in the PCB variant the upper limb nerves carry the abnormalities [EAN_PNS_2023, Wakerley_2014].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and excludes the infectious and malignant causes of polyradiculopathy that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR and MuSK antibodies negative, together with no decrement on repetitive stimulation, against bulbar myasthenia gravis
action_criteria.label: Acetylcholine receptor and MuSK antibodies to exclude bulbar myasthenia gravis
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar and neck-arm weakness without sensory loss is the presentation of bulbar myasthenia gravis, the main mimic of the PCB variant [Wakerley_2014].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-GT1a IgG positive (1:320), anti-GQ1b negative: supports the PCB variant; a negative result would not exclude it
action_criteria.label: Serum anti-GT1a IgG (with anti-GQ1b) for the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant
action_criteria.rationale: Anti-GT1a IgG, often with anti-GQ1b, is the antibody of the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant (Wakerley 2014); EAN/PNS 2023 restricts ganglioside testing to the MFS spectrum and its regional variants. It supports the clinical diagnosis and does not delay treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Botulinum neurotoxin not detected in serum
action_criteria.label: Optional serum botulinum toxin assay for the descending bulbar mimic
action_criteria.rationale: Botulism is the descending bulbar mimic of the PCB variant; here normal pupils and eye movements, areflexia, a demyelinating NCS, raised CSF protein and no exposure already make it low, so the reference-laboratory assay is optional.

action_criteria.label: Brain MRI to exclude a brainstem lesion
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar-predominant weakness raises a brainstem lesion; a normal brain MRI removes it [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics (potassium, magnesium, CK) and give the baseline before IVIg [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar weakness with a weak cough is the main risk in the PCB variant; serial FVC, MIP and MEP guide ICU-level care and intubation planning [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 68-104 bpm with no pauses or arrhythmia and blood pressure 118/72 to 142/88 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm 96 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 438 ms) and no conduction or ST-T abnormality: a baseline while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No current medications, so no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check before IVIg or plasma exchange (no current medications)
action_criteria.rationale: He takes no medicines, so the check cannot change management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on immunotherapy in the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not delay IVIg while waiting for the send-out anti-GT1a and anti-GQ1b result.
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring: bulbar weakness with a weak cough and aspiration on thin liquids, FVC 2.8 L (67% predicted, 37 mL/kg), MIP -34 and MEP 46 cmH2O; repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Plan elective intubation if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (1.5 L at 75 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, or bulbar function, cough or secretions worsen; intubate at once for respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia.

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, 30 g/day at 75 kg) for progressive bulbar weakness with aspiration risk, although he still walks unaided; plasma exchange is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].
Nil by mouth until a formal swallow assessment confirms a safe swallow; nasogastric feeding in the meantime.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.

differential.key_features: Bulbar and neck-arm weakness fit, but there is no fatigability or ptosis, the weak arms are areflexic, NCS is demyelinating with no decrement on repetitive stimulation, and AChR and MuSK antibodies are negative.

Descending bulbar and arm weakness fits, but pupils and eye movements are normal, the NCS is demyelinating (botulism gives low CMAPs with normal velocities), CSF protein is raised, and there is no wound, food or honey exposure, and the serum botulinum toxin assay, if sent, is negative.
Symmetric lower motor neuron pattern with areflexia, no long-tract or crossed signs, and a normal brain MRI.
Palatal weakness can occur, but there was no pharyngitis or membrane, and the disease is rare where vaccination is routine.
Trismus and rigidity rather than weakness with areflexia.

key_clinical_evidence: The pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant is oropharyngeal, neck and arm weakness with arm areflexia and spared legs [Wakerley_2014]: here nasal dysarthria, dysphagia, neck flexion 3+/5, shoulder abduction 3/5, absent arm reflexes and 5/5 legs.

Anti-GT1a IgG (positive here at 1:320) supports the PCB variant but does not establish the diagnosis on its own; the CSF dissociation (protein 72 mg/dL, 3 cells/mm3) and the upper limb predominant demyelinating NCS do [EAN_PNS_2023].
Bulbar weakness with a weak cough calls for ICU-level monitoring even while limb strength and gait are preserved [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019].
Normal repetitive stimulation and negative AChR and MuSK antibodies with areflexic weak arms separate the PCB variant from bulbar myasthenia gravis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant spares the legs; areflexia in the weak arms, the CSF albuminocytological dissociation and the upper limb demyelinating NCS place the diagnosis within the GBS spectrum, and normal repetitive stimulation with negative AChR and MuSK antibodies argues against myasthenia gravis.
red_herrings.data_point: Absence of leg weakness with bulbar predominance
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest myasthenia gravis or brainstem disease rather than a regional GBS variant.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

metadata.difficulty_description: Atypical PCB variant with descending pattern and leg sparing: requires recognizing GBS without classic ascending paralysis
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry), 2 recommended mimic exclusions (AChR/MuSK antibodies, brain MRI), 1 red herring (leg sparing).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Five-day progressive dysphagia and arm weakness with nasal speech; gait preserved.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. D. is a 32-year-old graphic designer presenting with a 5-day history of progressive oropharyngeal and upper extremity weakness. He initially noticed mild difficulty swallowing solid food approximately 5 days ago, which has progressed to coughing on thin liquids. Two days ago, he developed bilateral arm weakness making it difficult to lift objects overhead or type at his workstation, and he has difficulty holding his head up. He recalls a low-grade fever with mild malaise approximately 10 days prior that he attributed to fatigue and resolved spontaneously without medical attention. He denies any bloody diarrhea or respiratory illness. He has no diplopia, no ptosis, and no leg weakness; he walked into the emergency department unassisted. His speech has a nasal quality and he cannot clear his throat effectively. He has no sensory symptoms. His partner noted that he had been having trouble buttoning his shirt for the past 3 days. He denies any prior neurological symptoms, and there is no family history of neuromuscular disease. He reports no wound, tick bite, home-canned food or honey ingestion.

neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact. Heel-shin intact. No cerebellar signs.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Nasal dysarthria. Dysphagia to solids and liquids; coughing on thin liquids. Bilateral palatal weakness; weak cough. No facial weakness. Pupils equal and reactive. No ptosis. Eye movements full, no ophthalmoplegia.
neurological_exam.motor: Neck flexion 3+/5, neck extension 4/5. Bilateral upper extremity weakness: shoulder abduction 3/5, elbow flexion 3+/5, grip 4/5. Lower extremity strength 5/5 bilaterally. Able to walk.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent bilateral biceps and brachioradialis. Trace patellar and Achilles bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Sensation intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration in all extremities.
